profile.headline: Applying Research @ The Solution Institution
profile.summary:
With a focus on saving our sponsors both time and money in regards to the acquisition choices they make, ELSYS evolves away from static document-centric process towards dynamic model-centric systems engineering tools. ELSYS systems engineering programs provide methodologies, tools, education, and leadership to support acquisition and life-cycle sustainment decisions. Our experts work across the acquisition phases to help decision makers optimize the design trade space for a spectrum on systems by providing tools to support the DoD Acquisition range of concerns, from blank sheet ideas to specific technology upgrades. We also work in the sustainment phases to model existing system architectures for technical baseline capture, enabling more agile upgrades and improved knowledge capture.

ELSYS is a leader in the development and application of Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE). The research and development of methods and application of MBSE spans from individual systems to systems-of-systems and family of systems across DoD and industry sponsors. One of our primary discriminators is how we combine software and systems engineering expertise to build, deliver, and facilitate the use of collaborative MBSE tools for our DoD acquisition and Program Management stakeholders. By combining commercially available tools and development of customer-tailored frameworks, ELSYS provides unique solutions to sponsors enabling their teams and projects to successfully execute modern systems engineering. ELSYS is a leader in the development of methods and automated frameworks to empower the use and application of MBSE, including the development of decision support toolsets, providing subject matter experts with the means to communicate the intricacies and impacts of decisions to senior leaders within an organization.

https://www.gtri.gatech.edu/focus-areas/applied-systems-engineering

•	8 years of enterprise cybersecurity experience. 
•	14 years of software development and software life cycle experience.
•	19 years of quality assurance experience in highly technical disciplines.
•	23 years of leadership and management experience.

positions.title: Hiring Our Heroes 22-3 Fellow (SkillBridge)
positions.description:
Hiring our Heroes 22-3 Fellowship at Georgia Tech Research Institute (GTRI) | ELSYS Lab/Systems Engineering Research (SER) Division 

• Shadowed Associate Division Chief, completed e-learning course for ISO 9001 quality management  system (QMS) for laboratory project management. Provided feedback for Project Initiation Meetings (PIMs), Monthly Project Status Reports (MPSRs), Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) Estimates. 
• Attended division strategy sessions to discuss organizational structure, current, and potential lines of business.
• Contributed to 3 Independent Research and Development (IRAD) efforts, used DOD experiences to inform and guide direction. 
• SER Division speaker for professional development "Lunch and Learn" hour. Authored and presented  lecture on Air Force and joint force organizational structure, history, and authorities. 
• Completed 1 week Fundamentals of Systems Engineering Course. Renewed understanding of systems engineering process and practiced analysis methods such as Technique for Order of Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS), Model Environment Decomposition, Process Decision Program Chart, Fault Tree Analysis, and Risk Matrix Mitigation.
• Shadowed Systems Engineering PHDs, assisted with knowledge capture during Goal Directed Task Analysis (GDTA) of Subject Matter Experts (SMEs) 
• Observed expert Model Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) efforts, tools, and methods. Obtained rudimentary knowledge of tools such as Cameo, DOORS, and MagicGrid. 
• Took initiative to self-study active lab projects and DOD acquisition frameworks such as DODI 5000.2

Completed R&R and Veteran transition training Apr-Jul, Hiring our Heroes interviews and Matching Jul-August, on site fellowship Sept-Nov.

positions.title: Platform Operations Manager
positions.description:
NCOIC (Non-Commissioned Officer in Charge) Platform Operations, Technical Operations Management Division - Joint Cyber Training Enterprise
•	Managed Persistent Cyber Training Environment Platform as a Service (PaaS) utilization and resource allocation serving the Cyber Workforce 
•	Mentored 5 company grade officers on Joint Exercise Life Cycle, Joint Training System, and full spectrum Cyber Operations 
•	Drove platform policy for and senior leader decision making for $987M contract 
•	Managed hybrid/remote workforce of 8 engineers, providing identity access management for 5 VMware stack based private clouds 
•	Provided exercise planning support for joint and international partner full spectrum cyber operations 
•	Shaped new joint org standup by defining non-material requirements, and acted as the primary trainer and sponsor to new expansion of military personnel that increased the size of the ops group by 75% 
•	Communicated and disseminated requirements to platform stakeholders, prioritized capabilities and created 8 software feature requests 
•	Operated under Agile Scrum Methodology participating as Product Owner, providing customer feedback to Project Managers and integrating platform teams into sprint planning.   
•	Assembled high performance team for in depth platform utilization and growth trajectory review to provide key metrics ultimately informing a $390M purchase decision, and a new pay-for-play cost model to expand DOD training capabilities to the entire cyber workforce.  
•	Leveraged software development experience to design and deploy a customer facing web portal supporting 300+ multi agency trusted agents for platform support.  
•	Organized platform conference, developed collaboration site, built automated reservation system, authored feedback form, vetted 28 presentations, reached 100+ organizations. 
•	Summit presentation speaker for new platform capability, led symposium on new automated resource allocation feature, reached 52 remote audiences.

positions.title: Cybersecurity Exercise Planner
positions.description:
NCOIC (Non-Commissioned Officer in Charge) Information Warfare Exercises | Weapons, Tactics, and Exercises | Joint Force Headquarters Cyber – Air Force 

•	Acted as AFCYBER/JFHQ-C (AF)/616OC “white cell”, managing internal/external exercise stimuli to achieve training objectives.
•	Conducted mission analysis/course of action development on Cyber Defense Operations Center concept integration; formalized unique cyber authority--shaped future for USAF Mission Defense Team employment 
•	Facilitates Joint Exercise Life Cycle (JELC) objectives, designs, develops, and executes Command Post, Table Top (TTX), and field exercises (FTX) 
•	Advises & integrates MAJCOM/DAF/CCMD exercise development to maximize audience engagement & minimize operations impact; Represented AFCYBER at 4 in person planning conference series 
•	Organized 3 cyber/C2 weapon system integrations, served as C2 Subject Matter Expert, enabled realistic cyber effects for Field training exercise 
•	Trained 21 Major Command Coordination Center/Mission Defense Teams on tasking/reporting sys; reconciled tactical operations procedures--fortified cyber 9-line incident event escalation process 
•	Supported Air Force Material Command infrastructure exercise; instructed 51 participants on CDOC functions—briefing Lauded by Air Force Institute of Technology and integrated into cyber curriculum 
•	Integrated 3 units into international field training exercise; leveraged exercise to certify 2 mission commanders--validated offensive cyber operation standardization 
•	Helmed AFCYBER use of USCC command and control system Project IKE; administered/managed 8 exercise instances/100+ accounts--developed 3 advanced operation report dashboards providing key metrics to executive leadership
•	Led 6-member cell in support of global exercises; oversaw 139 DCO/OCO responses—provided command and control / mission reporting realism for Combatant Command battle staff.

positions.title: NDE Specialist (Non-Destructive Engineering) / Field Engineer
positions.description: Served as an independent contractor managing a team of 2-5 laborers and specialists to conduct non-destructive testing in power plants, refineries, and commercial HVAC units. Responsible for managing travel, accommodations, equipment and supplies, customer briefings, bids, invoices, test preparation, team job and safety training, and report generation.  Supplied technical expertise for calibrating equipment and proper test execution according to customer requirements (typically ASME, American Society of Mechanical Engineers).  Primary specialty was eddy current heat exchanger tube analysis which involved reading an oscilloscope and using a CAD software to draw tube sheet layouts for data collection and report generation.  Also conducted and held LVL II certifications in magnetic particle, dye penetrant, and ultrasonic testing.

honors.title: GTRI STAR Award
honors.description: GTRI’s leadership would like to extend their congratulations to employees who received a GTRI Star Performer Award for the performance period of April 1, 2024 – May 31, 2024. The Star Performer Award is part of the University System of Georgia’s (USG) Incentive, Compensation, and Reward Policy that rewards exceptional performance in response to anticipated events and circumstances impacting GTRI. All employees nominated and selected as winners demonstrated performance above and beyond their normal job expectations; and efforts supported GTRI’s Strategic Goals: Impact, Inclusion, Agility, People-First, and/or Innovation within the organization.
honors.issuer: Issued by Georgia Tech Research Institute · Apr 2024

honors.title: THE AIR AND SPACE COMMENDATION MEDAL
honors.description: Technical Sergeant David Campbell distinguished himself by meritorious service as Noncommissioned Officer in Charge, Info Warfare Exercises, 616th Operations Center, 16th Air Force, Joint Base San Antonio-Lackland, Texas. During this period, Sergeant Campbell led the Offensive Cyber Operations team, overseeing the execution of 8,500 missions that delivered payloads to 639,000 targets in support of four joint task forces. As the sole offensive cyber evaluator, he increased manning by sixty-six percent by certifying additional controllers. His coordination of cyber effects resulted in the liberation of fifty-three coalition prisoners, and the capture or kill of thirty-four high value individuals. Additionally, Sergeant Campbell managed the first United States Cyber Command counter-interference campaign, securing the 2018 United States elections and earning the Operations Center 2018 Team of the Year award. Furthermore, Sergeant Campbell represented Air Forces Cyber at four joint planning conferences, where he was instrumental in developing seventy training scenarios across five exercises, supporting training objectives for 26,000 individuals. Finally, Sergeant Campbell was the subject matter expert of full spectrum cyber operations for joint cyber training under United States Cyber Command. His expertise drove policy and aided senior leader decisions on a joint cyber platform contract valued at 390 million dollars. The distinctive accomplishments of Sergeant Campbell while serving his country reflect credit upon himself and the United States Air Force.
honors.issuer: Issued by JUSTIN P. MOKROVICH, Colonel, USAF · Nov 2022
